title: Who visits Malaysia?
subtitle: Half of all arrivals come from one country next door: Singapore.
question: Where do Malaysia's foreign visitors come from?
answer: Mostly from next door. In a typical month Malaysia welcomes around 3 million foreign visitors, and about half of them are Singaporeans crossing the causeway. Indonesia and China are next, but nobody comes close to Singapore. Malaysia's busiest border is a land bridge, not an airport.

takeaways: **Half of Malaysia's visitors are Singaporeans**: about 1.56 million in October 2024 alone, crossing the causeway to shop, eat and visit family.
The rest of the top ranks are **regional neighbours**: Indonesia (10.9%), Thailand (6.0%) and Brunei (3.2%). Proximity beats everything.
**China is the big long-haul source** at about 10%, far ahead of any Western country.
The **top four are all Asian and make up 77%** of arrivals. Western visitors (UK, Australia, US) are a small slice each.
It reframes 'tourism': Malaysia's visitor economy is overwhelmingly a **short-haul, neighbourhood** one, not a long-haul destination story.

faq.a: About 3.1 million foreign arrivals in October 2024, the latest published month, according to Immigration Department data on data.gov.my. Annual arrivals run into the tens of millions.

faq.q: Which country do most Malaysia visitors come from?
faq.a: Singapore, by a huge margin: around 50% of all foreign arrivals (about 1.56 million in October 2024), mostly crossing the land border. Indonesia (~11%) and China (~10%) are next.

faq.q: How many Chinese tourists visit Malaysia?
faq.a: China made up about 10% of foreign arrivals in October 2024, the largest long-haul source and third overall behind Singapore and Indonesia.

faq.q: Where does this tourism data come from?
faq.a: From the Immigration Department of Malaysia (arrivals by nationality), published as official open data on data.gov.my. Figures are for October 2024, the latest published month.
